angle: Why a Python extension can change the runtime mode

items.claim: CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration that can disable the GIL.
items.synthesisExcerpt: CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the global interpreter lock disabled.
items.sourceEvidence: “CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the global interpreter lock disabled.”
items.qualification: Keep the claim specific to CPython 3.13.

items.claim: An extension must declare support for free threading; importing one without that declaration warns and enables the GIL.
items.synthesisExcerpt: An extension must explicitly indicate that it supports this mode; importing one without that declaration warns and enables the GIL.
items.sourceEvidence: “An extension must explicitly indicate that it supports this mode; importing one without that declaration warns and enables the GIL.”
items.usefulness: Connects extension compatibility to observable import behavior.
items.qualification: The described fallback applies when the declaration is absent.

items.claim: Declaring free-threading support is distinct from making code thread-safe.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Free threading is a configuration, and a support declaration is distinct from the work of making code thread-safe.
items.sourceEvidence: “Free threading is a configuration, and a support declaration is distinct from the work of making code thread-safe.”
items.usefulness: Clarifies the separate responsibility extension authors have.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not describe the work needed to make code thread-safe.

items.claim: The support mechanism differs for multi-phase and single-phase extension initialization.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The mechanism differs between extensions using multi-phase and single-phase initialization.
items.sourceEvidence: “The mechanism differs between extensions using multi-phase and single-phase initialization.”
items.usefulness: Signals that the import-boundary detail depends on initialization style.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not specify either mechanism.

items.claim: On Windows, extension builds do not automatically receive the Py_GIL_DISABLED macro from the compiler.
items.synthesisExcerpt: On Windows the compiler does not get the Py_GIL_DISABLED macro automatically for extension builds;
items.sourceEvidence: “On Windows the compiler does not get the Py_GIL_DISABLED macro automatically for extension builds”
items.qualification: This detail is specific to Windows extension builds.

items.claim: The configuration can be checked via sysconfig.
items.synthesisExcerpt: the configuration can be checked via sysconfig.
items.sourceEvidence: “the configuration can be checked via sysconfig.”
items.usefulness: Provides a way to inspect the configuration.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not give a specific sysconfig command.
